papers.title: Gaussian Process (GP)-based Learning Control of Selective Laser Melting Process
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) is one of emerging processes for effective metal additive manufacturing. Due to complex heat exchange and material phase changes, it is challenging to accurately model the SLM dynamics and design robust control of SLM process. In this paper, we first present a data-driven Gaussian process based dynamic model for SLM process and then design a model predictive control to regulate the melt pool size. Physical and process constraints are considered in the controller design. The learning model and control design are tested and validated with high-fidelity finite element simulation. The comparison results with other control design demonstrate the efficacy of the control design.

summary_en.motivation: Accurate modeling and robust control of the Selective Laser Melting process are challenging due to complex heat transfer and phase changes.
summary_en.method: A Gaussian process-based data-driven dynamic model is developed and integrated with model predictive control to regulate melt pool size subject to physical and process constraints.
summary_en.result: The proposed control design effectively regulates melt pool dimensions while satisfying constraints, outperforming baseline controllers in simulation.
summary_en.validation: The learning model and control strategy are validated using high-fidelity finite element simulations of the SLM process.

papers.title: Smooth Variational Graph Embeddings for Efficient Neural Architecture Search
papers.abstract: Neural architecture search (NAS) has recently been addressed from various directions, including discrete, sampling-based methods and efficient differentiable approaches. While the former are notoriously expensive, the latter suffer from imposing strong constraints on the search space. Architecture optimization from a learned embedding space for example through graph neural network based variational autoencoders builds a middle ground and leverages advantages from both sides. Such approaches have recently shown good performance on several benchmarks. Yet, their stability and predictive power heavily depends on their capacity to reconstruct networks from the embedding space. In this paper, we propose a two-sided variational graph autoencoder, which allows to smoothly encode and accurately reconstruct neural architectures from various search spaces. We evaluate the proposed approach on neural architectures defined by the ENAS approach, the NAS-Bench-101 and the NAS-Bench-201 search space and show that our smooth embedding space allows to directly extrapolate the performance prediction to architectures outside the seen domain (e.g. with more operations). Thus, it facilitates to predict good network architectures even without expensive Bayesian optimization or reinforcement learning.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究神经架构搜索，与有限元代理模型或植入物设计完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on neural architecture search for neural networks, not on surrogate modeling for finite element analysis or biomechanical design; it lacks any connection to physical simulation, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or implant mechanics.

summary_en.motivation: To improve efficiency and generalization of neural architecture search by learning smooth embeddings.
summary_en.method: A two-sided variational graph autoencoder is proposed to encode and reconstruct neural architectures smoothly.
summary_en.result: The smooth embedding enables direct performance extrapolation to architectures outside the training domain without expensive optimization.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on standard NAS benchmarks including ENAS, NAS-Bench-101, and NAS-Bench-201.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Gaussian Process Regression for Probabilistic States Estimation and Forecasting in Power Grids
papers.abstract: Real-time state estimation and forecasting is critical for efficient operation of power grids. In this paper, a physics-informed Gaussian process regression (PhI-GPR) method is presented and used for probabilistic forecasting and estimating the phase angle, angular speed, and wind mechanical power of a three-generator power grid system using sparse measurements. In standard data-driven Gaussian process regression (GPR), parameterized models for the prior statistics are fit by maximizing the marginal likelihood of observed data, whereas in PhI-GPR, we compute the prior statistics by solving stochastic equations governing power grid dynamics. The short-term forecast of a power grid system dominated by wind generation is complicated by the stochastic nature of the wind and the resulting uncertain mechanical wind power. Here, we assume that the power-grid dynamic is governed by the swing equations, and we treat the unknown terms in the swing equations (specifically, the mechanical wind power) as random processes, which turns these equations into stochastic differential equations. We solve these equations for the mean and variance of the power grid system using the Monte Carlo simulations method. We demonstrate that the proposed PhI-GPR method can accurately forecast and estimate both observed and unobserved states, including the mean behavior and associated uncertainty. For observed states, we show that PhI-GPR provides a forecast comparable to the standard data-driven GPR, with both forecasts being significantly more accurate than the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) forecast. We also show that the ARIMA forecast is much more sensitive to observation frequency and measurement errors than the PhI-GPR forecast.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的物理信息高斯过程回归方法具有不确定性量化能力，但应用领域为电力系统而非生物力学设计，方法可迁移但非直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling, structural mechanics, or implant/biomechanics design; its application is power grid state estimation with no solid mechanics or design optimization.

summary_zh.method: 基于随机摆动方程的物理信息高斯过程回归，用蒙特卡洛求解统计量
summary_zh.result: 准确预测相角、角速度和风力机械功率的均值与不确定性
summary_zh.validation: 与标准高斯过程和ARIMA对比，蒙特卡洛仿真验证

summary_en.motivation: Accurate probabilistic state estimation and forecasting in power grids with sparse measurements and stochastic wind integration.
summary_en.method: A physics-informed Gaussian process regression (PhI-GPR) that computes prior statistics by solving stochastic swing equations via Monte Carlo simulation.
summary_en.result: PhI-GPR yields accurate mean and uncertainty forecasts for both observed and unobserved states, outperforming ARIMA and matching standard GPR.
summary_en.validation: Validation through Monte Carlo simulations comparing to standard GPR and ARIMA on a three-generator system.

papers.title: Robust walking based on MPC with viability guarantees
papers.abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has shown great success for controlling complex systems such as legged robots. However, when closing the loop, the performance and feasibility of the finite horizon optimal control problem (OCP) solved at each control cycle is not guaranteed anymore. This is due to model discrepancies, the effect of low-level controllers, uncertainties and sensor noise. To address these issues, we propose a modified version of a standard MPC approach used in legged locomotion with viability (weak forward invariance) guarantees. In this approach, instead of adding a (conservative) terminal constraint to the problem, we propose to use the measured state projected to the viability kernel in the OCP solved at each control cycle. Moreover, we use past experimental data to find the best cost weights, which measure a combination of performance, constraint satisfaction robustness, or stability (invariance). These interpretable costs measure the trade off between robustness and performance. For this purpose, we use Bayesian optimization (BO) to systematically design experiments that help efficiently collect data to learn a cost function leading to robust performance. Our simulation results with different realistic disturbances (i.e. external pushes, unmodeled actuator dynamics and computational delay) show the effectiveness of our approach to create robust controllers for humanoid robots.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注机器人行走控制，与FEA和代理模型无直接关联，但其贝叶斯优化方法可能为设计空间探索提供思路。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, or biomechanical implant design.

summary_zh.method: 使用投影到生存核的状态和贝叶斯优化调整成本权重。
summary_zh.result: 仿真表明该方法能有效提高对外部扰动和未建模动态的鲁棒性。
summary_zh.validation: 在仿真环境中施加多种干扰（推力、未建模执行器动态等）验证控制器性能。

summary_en.motivation: To address performance and feasibility degradation of MPC under model discrepancies and uncertainties in legged locomotion.
summary_en.method: Projects measured states onto the viability kernel and uses Bayesian optimization to tune cost weights from experimental data.
summary_en.result: Simulation results demonstrate improved robustness against external pushes, unmodeled actuator dynamics, and computational delay.
summary_en.validation: Validated through simulations with realistic disturbances including external pushes and unmodeled actuator dynamics.

papers.title: Model Exploration with Cost-Aware Learning
papers.abstract: We present an extension to active learning routines in which non-constant costs are explicitly considered. This work considers both known and unknown costs and introduces the term ε-frugal for learners that do not only consider minimizing total costs but are also able to explore high cost regions of the sample space. We demonstrate our extension on a well-known machine learning dataset and find that out ε-frugal learners outperform both learners with known costs and random sampling.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法可能在代理模型的主动学习中有潜在应用，但未涉及生物力学或有限元问题。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA or surrogate modeling application, no constraint handling or uncertainty quantification, and tested only on a standard ML dataset without biomedical or implant context.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决主动学习中非恒定成本的采样效率问题。
summary_zh.method: 提出ε-节俭学习器，显式考虑已知和未知成本。
summary_zh.result: 在标准数据集上，ε-节俭学习器优于已知成本或随机采样。
summary_zh.validation: 在标准机器学习数据集上进行性能对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve active learning efficiency by explicitly accounting for non-constant sampling costs.
summary_en.method: Introduces ε-frugal learners that balance total cost minimization with exploration of high-cost regions.
summary_en.result: Experiments on a standard ML dataset show ε-frugal learners outperform both known-cost and random sampling baselines.
summary_en.validation: Validated on a well-known machine learning benchmark dataset.

papers.title: MIMO ILC for Precision SEA robots using Input-weighted Complex-Kernel Regression
papers.abstract: This work improves the positioning precision of lightweight robots with series elastic actuators (SEAs). Lightweight SEA robots, along with low-impedance control, can maneuver without causing damage in uncertain, confined spaces such as inside an aircraft wing during aircraft assembly. Nevertheless, substantial modeling uncertainties in SEA robots reduce the precision achieved by model-based approaches such as inversion-based feedforward. Therefore, this article improves the precision of SEA robots around specified operating points, through a multi-input multi-output (MIMO), iterative learning control (ILC) approach. The main contributions of this article are to (i) introduce an input-weighted complex kernel to estimate local MIMO models using complex Gaussian process regression (c-GPR) (ii) develop Geršgorin-theorem-based conditions on the iteration gains for ensuring ILC convergence to precision within noise-related limits, even with errors in the estimated model; and (iii) demonstrate precision positioning with an experimental SEA robot. Comparative experimental results, with and without ILC, show around 90% improvement in the positioning precision (close to the repeatability limit of the robot) and a 10-times increase in the SEA robot's operating speed with the use of the MIMO ILC.

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文研究的是机器人控制，与有限元代理模型和植入物设计方向无关。

summary_en.result: Achieved approximately 90% improvement in positioning precision and a 10-fold increase in operating speed.
summary_en.validation: Comparative experiments on an actual SEA robot with and without ILC.

papers.title: Investigation of Bone Growth in Additive-Manufactured Pedicle Screw Implant by Using Ti-6Al-4V and Bioactive Glass Powder Composite.
papers.abstract: In this study, we optimized the geometry and composition of additive-manufactured pedicle screws. Metal powders of titanium-aluminum-vanadium (Ti-6Al-4V) were mixed with reactive glass-ceramic biomaterials of bioactive glass (BG) powders. To optimize the geometry of pedicle screws, we applied a novel numerical approach to proposing the optimal shape of the healing chamber to promote biological healing. We examined the geometry and composition effects of pedicle screw implants on the interfacial autologous bone attachment and bone graft incorporation through in vivo studies. The addition of an optimal amount of BG to Ti-6Al-4V leads to a lower elastic modulus of the ceramic-metal composite material, effectively reducing the stress-shielding effects. Pedicle screw implants with optimal shape design and made of the composite material of Ti-6Al-4V doped with BG fabricated through additive manufacturing exhibit greater osseointegration and a more rapid bone volume fraction during the fracture healing process 120 days after implantation, per in vivo studies.

summary_en.motivation: To optimize the geometry and composition of additive-manufactured pedicle screws for enhanced bone healing and reduced stress shielding.
summary_en.method: Ti-6Al-4V powder was mixed with bioactive glass, the screw shape was numerically optimized, and implants were fabricated via additive manufacturing and tested in an animal model.
summary_en.result: The composite with optimal bioactive glass content exhibited lower elastic modulus, reduced stress shielding, and improved osseointegration and bone volume fraction at 120 days post-implantation.
summary_en.validation: In vivo study using a sheep model with histological and radiographic evaluation at 120 days.
